steps.explain: Angle B is smaller than a right angle (it fits inside a square corner), so it is acute.
Angle C is wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse (between 90° and 180°).
So only angle A is a right angle.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one is a different type or size of angle; compare them with 90° and 180° to see why they do not match.

keyPoints.note: A right angle is exactly 90°.
Compare each picture with a right angle and a straight line.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.

Why the other answers are wrong: each one is a different type or size of angle; compare them with 90° and 180° to see why they do not match.

keyPoints.note: Compare the angle with 90° and 180°.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.

steps.explain: So the angle is a obtuse angle. (acute < 90°, right = 90°, obtuse 90°–180°, straight = 180°, reflex 180°–360°.)
Why the other answers are wrong: each one is a different type or size of angle; compare them with 90° and 180° to see why they do not match.

keyPoints.note: Compare the angle with 90° and 180°.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.

steps.explain: There are 12 numbers on a clock face and a full turn is 360°, so the gap between neighbouring numbers is 360° ÷ \(12 = 30\)°.
The hands are 6 number gaps apart (the smaller angle between the hands).
180° is exactly 180°, so the hands make a straight angle.

steps.explain: Both angles are 45°. Check: they are acute (less than 90°), and 45° is half of a right angle, so the answer is sensible.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one is a different type or size of angle; compare them with 90° and 180° to see why they do not match.

keyPoints.note: Compare with a right angle first.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.

steps.explain: The vertex is at the bottom. One arm points straight up, the other leans to the right. The curved arrow shows the angle between them.

steps.explain: Check: 60° is acute. The vertical arm is 90° from the horizontal and the leaning arm is 30° from the horizontal, so 90° − 30° = 60°.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one is a different type or size of angle; compare them with 90° and 180° to see why they do not match.

keyPoints.note: Compare with a right angle first.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.

steps.explain: The protractor shows only the part past the straight line, so add 180° to it.
This is a 240° angle. Check: it is between 180° and 360°, so it is a reflex angle.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one is a different type or size of angle; compare them with 90° and 180° to see why they do not match.

keyPoints.note: Compare with a right angle first.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 10: Lines and angles

steps.explain: The other arm crosses the scale at 90°.
The estimate and the measurement agree: the angle is 90°, a right angle.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one is a different type or size of angle; compare them with 90° and 180° to see why they do not match.

keyPoints.note: Line up the 0° line with one arm and the centre with the vertex.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.

meta.source: ICE-EM Mathematics Year 6 (3rd ed.) Chapter 10: Lines and angles

keyPoints.note: A reflex angle is between 180° and 360°.
Compare each picture with a right angle and a straight line.
An angle is the amount of turn between two arms.
